posts.title: GSTR-1 vs GSTR-3B: Differences and How They Should Match
posts.description: GSTR-1 reports your sales invoice by invoice; GSTR-3B is the summary return where tax is paid. See how they differ, their due dates and why they must match.
posts.h1: GSTR-1 vs GSTR-3B: what each return reports and how they should match
posts.summary: GSTR-1 lists your outward supplies invoice by invoice. GSTR-3B is the summary return in which you declare liability, claim input tax credit (ITC) and pay tax. The sales figures in the two returns should agree.

blocks.v: The short difference

head: GSTR-1
GSTR-3B
rows: Outward supplies (sales), invoice-wise and by type
Summary of outward supplies, ITC claimed and tax payable
Gives your buyers their GSTR-2A/2B data and the department your sales detail
Declares liability and is the return through which tax is paid
13th of the month after the quarter
22nd or 24th of the month after the quarter, by state category
Your customers, because their ITC depends on it
You, because tax is paid with it

blocks.v: Why your customers care about GSTR-1

The invoices you report in GSTR-1 flow into your buyers' auto-drafted GSTR-2B. If an invoice is missed or reported with the wrong GSTIN or value, your buyer may not see the credit they expect. That leads to calls from customers asking you to correct the return.
Why the two returns must agree

GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B are compared by the system. In recent years GSTN has moved towards auto-populating GSTR-3B from GSTR-1, so an error in GSTR-1 can carry into GSTR-3B. A mismatch between sales in the two returns can lead to a notice, so it is worth checking before you file.
A quick pre-filing check

v: Compare total taxable value and tax in GSTR-1 with the outward supply table in GSTR-3B
Check that credit notes and amendments are included in the right period
Look at invoices reported in the wrong month or under the wrong GSTIN
Confirm that e-invoices match what you report in GSTR-1
Keep a note of the reason for any difference you decide to carry forward

blocks.v: How TaxPower GST helps
TaxPower GST lets you compare GSTR-3B with GSTR-1 in one preview, download GSTR-1 data and compare GSTR-1 with e-invoices to find missing invoices and tax differences before you file.

posts.title: GSTR-2B ITC Reconciliation Checklist for CAs and Businesses
posts.description: A step-by-step checklist to reconcile your purchase register with GSTR-2B: match invoices, sort differences, follow up suppliers and claim ITC with confidence.
posts.h1: GSTR-2B ITC reconciliation: a step-by-step checklist
posts.summary: ITC reconciliation compares the purchase invoices in your books with the invoices your suppliers have reported, which appear in your GSTR-2B. Work through the differences before you claim credit in GSTR-3B.

blocks.v: Step 1: get both sets of data
Download GSTR-2B for the month and export your purchase register from your accounts. Check that both cover the same period and the same GSTIN.
Step 2: match invoices

Match on supplier GSTIN and invoice number first, then compare date, taxable value and tax. Small differences such as extra spaces or prefixes in invoice numbers are a common reason for false mismatches, so a good tool normalises them.
Step 3: sort the differences

head: Result
What it usually means
What to do
rows: Invoice is in both books and GSTR-2B
Claim ITC, subject to the usual conditions
Data entry difference or supplier error
Confirm with the invoice and the supplier
Supplier has not filed or reported it yet
Follow up with the supplier; do not rush to claim
Purchase not booked, or booked in another period
Check and book the invoice if it is yours

blocks.v: Step 4: check what ITC you are allowed to claim
Matching an invoice does not by itself make the credit eligible. Credits that are blocked or conditional under the GST law still need your review, and your CA can advise on the treatment.
Step 5: handle IMS actions

With the Invoice Management System (IMS), the recipient can accept, reject or keep pending invoices before GSTR-2B is generated. Decide on each invoice, keep a record of why, and revisit pending ones in later months.
Step 6: keep a record
Save the reconciliation report with the return working papers. It is your evidence if a notice later questions the credit you claimed.
How TaxPower GST helps
TaxPower GST imports your purchase register, compares it with GSTR-2B, shows matched invoices and differences and lets you export audit-ready reports to Excel.

posts.title: Form 16 and Form 16A (Forms 130 and 131) Explained
posts.description: What Form 16, Form 16A and Form 27D are, who issues them, how they are generated from TRACES and the new form numbers 130, 131 and 133.
posts.h1: Form 16 and Form 16A explained, with the new form numbers
posts.summary: TDS certificates are proof that tax was deducted and deposited. Form 16 is for salary, Form 16A for other TDS and Form 27D for TCS.

blocks.v: The three certificates

head: Earlier form
New form
Certificate for
rows: Salary TDS, issued to the employee
TDS on non-salary payments, issued to the deductee

blocks.v: How they are produced

Certificates are generated from data in TRACES after the quarterly statement has been filed and processed. Form 16 has two parts: Part A comes from TRACES and Part B contains the salary and tax computation. The certificate must be signed, usually digitally.
When to issue them

Form 16 for a year is due by 15 June after the year ends. Form 16A is due within a fixed number of days after the quarterly statement due date, which is usually 15 August, 15 November, 15 February and 15 June. Confirm the dates for your year on the Income Tax portal.
Common problems

v: The statement has not been processed, so no certificate is available yet
PAN of the deductee is wrong or inoperative
The challan used is unmatched in the statement
Part B details of the employee are missing

posts.title: How to Choose GST Software for a CA Practice: 8 Questions
posts.description: Eight practical questions to ask before buying GST software: multi-client work, reconciliation, e-invoicing, portal filing, support, price and trial.
posts.h1: How to choose GST software for a CA practice: 8 questions to ask
posts.summary: Use these questions to compare GST software on what matters in daily work. Ask for a trial and test them on your own clients' data.

blocks.v: 1. Can it manage many GSTINs from one place?
A practice needs a single view of return status and filing dates across all clients, with search and filters.
2. Can it file directly to the portal?
Look for upload and download from inside the software, with EVC/OTP or DSC support, so that you do not log in to the portal client by client.
3. How good is ITC reconciliation?
Test GSTR-2B reconciliation with a messy purchase register. Check how it handles invoice-number differences and whether IMS actions are supported.
4. Does it cover e-invoice and e-way bill?
If your clients raise e-invoices, bulk generation and an e-way bill from an IRN save a lot of time.
5. What reports do you get?
Good reports include form-wise previews, GSTR-3B vs GSTR-1 comparison, party-wise and rate-wise summaries and Excel exports.
6. Who supports you, and in which language?
Ask where the support team is, the hours they work and whether they help in the language your staff are comfortable with.
7. What does it really cost?
Compare the installation fee, the yearly renewal, charges for extra users and the GST on top. Ask what is included in the first year.
8. Can you try it first?
A free trial lets you test the questions above on your own work. TaxPower GST has a 30-day free trial.
